overview.title: Overview
overview.byCategoryEmpty: Once you import transactions, you’ll see where your money goes here.
overview.getStartedHint: Three steps to a working budget.
overview.stepBackupBody: Encrypted, daily, to a folder or drive you choose.
overview.stepAccountsBody: Give each account a name, and the bank if you like.
overview.stepImportBody: Kasboek reads it and shows every row before anything is saved.
overview.noBudgets: No budgets set for this month
overview.uncategorized_one: {{count}} transaction this month has no category yet.
overview.uncategorized_other: {{count}} transactions this month have no category yet.
overview.trendHint: Income and spending, transfers between your own accounts left out.
overview.reviewPrompt: Review {{month}} for me (use summary_review for {{iso}}). How did income and spending compare with earlier months, which categories changed most, which budgets went over, and which payments stand out? End with one or two practical tips. Keep it short.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.subtitle: Every payment in and out, across all accounts.
transactions.emptyBody: Import a CSV export from your bank to get started.
transactions.refundHint: Money back in a spending category (a refund, or someone paying their share) lowers that spending; it doesn’t count as income.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.hint: Spending counts money out minus refunds. Transfers between your own accounts don’t count.
budgets.emptyHint: No budgets for this month yet. Type an amount next to a category, or copy last month’s.
budgets.rulesHint: Rules put transactions in a category automatically when the text matches. They apply to imports and, when created, to uncategorised transactions.
budgets.rulesOrder: When several rules match, the one highest in this list wins.
budgets.reach_one: Matches {{count}} transaction, {{uncategorised}} of them without a category.
budgets.reach_other: Matches {{count}} transactions, {{uncategorised}} of them without a category.
budgets.reachOther_one: {{count}} is already in another category and stays there.
budgets.reachOther_other: {{count}} are already in another category and stay there.
budgets.reachWord: Short texts only match as a whole word.
budgets.ibanHint: The counterparty’s account number, exactly. Good for transfers to your own accounts.

import.title: Import
import.subtitle: Bring in CSV exports from your bank. Nothing is saved until you approve.
import.dropBody: Kasboek reads the file, recognises the bank, flags duplicates and problems, and suggests categories. You review everything before it’s saved.
import.needAccount: Add the bank account first, so Kasboek knows where these transactions belong.
import.undoConfirm_one: Remove the {{count}} transaction from this import?
import.undoConfirm_other: Remove the {{count}} transactions from this import?
import.noMapping: Kasboek couldn’t tell which columns hold the date and amount. Choose them under Columns.

issue.possible_duplicate: looks like a transaction already in Kasboek

import.columnsHint: Tell Kasboek which column holds what. The first row of data is shown in brackets.
import.invert: Flip signs (money out is positive in this file)
import.fixAmount: Enter the amount, negative for money out (e.g. -12,50)
import.checked: {{ai}} checked the file. See the notes above the rows.
import.checkPrivacy: Sends the rows of this file to {{aiCompany}}.
import.claudeOff: Set up an assistant in Settings to have it check files.
import.anyBank: Works with CSV exports from any bank: Kasboek reads the column names (Dutch, French, English or German) and remembers each layout after the first import.
import.checkPrivacyLocal: Sends the rows of this file to {{ai}} on this computer or network.
import.checkSlowHint: Large files are checked in parts, a few at a time. Each part stops by itself after 4 minutes.
import.allKnown: Everything in this file is already in Kasboek ({{from}} – {{to}}).
import.allKnownHint: {{name}} can still sort the transactions of this account that have no category yet.

check.title: What {{name}} did
check.already: {{count}} of {{total}} rows were already in Kasboek and weren’t checked again.
check.renamed_one: Made the name or description readable for {{count}} row
check.renamed_other: Made the name or description readable for {{count}} rows
check.nothingChanged: Nothing in this file needed changing.
check.proposals: Suggestions (only applied when you accept them)
check.rulesTitle: Rules, so future imports are categorised automatically
check.skippedSince_one: {{count}} already had a category by then and was left alone.
check.skippedSince_other: {{count}} already had a category by then and were left alone.
check.saved: Saved: {{rules}} rule(s) and {{count}} categorised transaction(s). Undoing the check doesn’t undo these; change them in Rules or Transactions.

import.transfersPaired_one: {{count}} transfer between your accounts was paired.
import.transfersPaired_other: {{count}} transfers between your accounts were paired.
import.transfersSuggested_one: {{count}} possible transfer to check under Transactions → Transfers.
import.transfersSuggested_other: {{count}} possible transfers to check under Transactions → Transfers.

assistant.title: {{ai}}
assistant.intro: Ask about your money, or let {{ai}} make changes. Anything that changes your data waits for your OK.
assistant.example1: How much did I spend on groceries last month?
assistant.example2: Set my eating-out budget to €150 a month.
assistant.example3: Put my uncategorised transactions in the right categories.
assistant.setupBody: Connect an AI assistant (Claude, Mistral, Gemini, a local model and more) to ask questions about your budget, set budgets, sort transactions and check CSV files.
assistant.privacy: Your messages, and the data {{ai}} looks up to answer them, are sent to {{aiCompany}}. Nothing is sent until you ask something.
assistant.privacyLocal: {{ai}} runs on this computer or your network: your messages and data are sent only there.
assistant.checkDone: Checked {{file}}: {{categorised}} categorised, {{renamed}} renamed, {{rules}} rules and {{existing}} older groups suggested. See the import screen.
assistant.reasoningHint: How much the model thinks before answering: less is faster and cheaper, more helps with harder questions. Not every model has this setting; if a model refuses it, Kasboek asks without it.
assistant.reasoningUnsupported: This model doesn't take a reasoning setting and uses its own.

settings.title: Settings
settings.ibanOptional: Optional. Helps match transfers between your own accounts.
settings.languageHint: Also used for month names. Number and date formats are set separately.
settings.backupsHint: Automatic, encrypted backups in the same format as an export. They open only with Import and your login.
settings.autoHint: Encrypted backups to a folder you choose. A synced folder (OneDrive, iCloud Drive, Dropbox) or a USB drive works well.
settings.securityHint: How your data is protected on this computer.
settings.keyStorageWeak: Not protected: no system keyring found
settings.keyStorageWeakHint: On Linux, install and unlock GNOME Keyring or KWallet, then restart Kasboek.
settings.passwordlessExplain: You’ll unlock Kasboek with {{name}} instead of a password. Your password stops working. A password is stronger: passwordless relies on your computer account.
settings.oldExportsNote: Exports and backups made earlier keep opening with the password that was current then.
settings.twoFactorHint: A 6-digit code from your phone, at every unlock and import.
settings.twoFactorOffBody: Enter a current code to confirm.
settings.recoveryHint: For a forgotten password or lost phone. Making a new one makes the old one stop working on this computer.
settings.newRecoveryBody: The current recovery key will stop working here. Exports made earlier still open with the old one.
settings.autoLockHint: Also locks when the screen locks or the computer sleeps.
settings.encryptionHint: Your budget data is encrypted on disk.
settings.keyStorageOsHint: Data is locked to this computer and user account.
settings.rememberedHint: Remembered on this computer until {{date}}. Other computers, imports and exports still ask for the code.
settings.forgotten: This computer will ask for the code again.
settings.whenBackupHint: Shortly after imports, restores and big changes, at most hourly after other changes, daily regardless, and when Kasboek locks or closes. Kept: everything from the last 24 hours, one per day for 30 days, one per month for a year.
settings.bankNameHint: Optional. Any bank, as you call it.
settings.formatsHint: Each part can be set on its own. Example: {{value}}
settings.accountCurrencyChange: Its {{from}} transactions will count as {{to}}. Use this to correct a wrong currency.
settings.accountKindInvestment: Record its value now and then on the Net worth page; deposits and withdrawals come from its transactions.

auth.welcomeBody: Your budget stays on this computer, encrypted. First, choose how you’ll unlock it.
auth.welcomeLegacy: Your existing data will be kept. Choose how you’ll unlock it from now on.
auth.choosePasswordBody: Strongest option. Works on every computer.
auth.chooseDeviceBody: Passwordless: unlock with your face, fingerprint or PIN.
auth.chooseImportBody: Open an export made with Kasboek, using its login details.
auth.passwordIntro: Use at least 16 characters. Easiest: a few random words with a capital and a number, like kraan-tulp-Ober-7-fiets-mist. Don’t use it anywhere else.
auth.recoveryBody: If you forget your password or lose your phone, this key is the only way back in. It’s shown once.
auth.recoveryTip1: Write it on paper, or store it in a password manager.
auth.recoveryTip2: Don’t keep it in a file on this computer.
auth.recoveryTip3: Kasboek can’t show it again. You can make a new one in Settings.
auth.recoverySaved: I’ve stored my recovery key somewhere safe.
auth.recoveryConfirm: Type the last group of 4 characters to confirm
auth.copied: Copied. Paste it somewhere safe, then clear your clipboard.
auth.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy. Please write it down.
auth.totpBody: Recommended. Besides your password, you’ll enter a 6-digit code from an app on your phone.
auth.totpStep1: Open an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password, …).
auth.totpStep2: Scan this code, or type the key.
auth.totpStep3: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows
auth.totpLater: You can change this later in Settings → Security.
auth.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
auth.recoveryUnlockBody: Enter the recovery key you saved when you set up Kasboek. You’ll choose a new password next.
auth.recoveredBody: You unlocked with your recovery key. Choose a new password to keep Kasboek secure.
auth.eraseBody: Deletes all Kasboek data on this computer. It can’t be undone. Exports and backups elsewhere are not touched.
auth.deviceUnavailableHint: Needs Windows Hello or Touch ID, which aren’t available on this computer.
auth.ruleVariety: Three of: lowercase, capitals, numbers, symbols
auth.ruleCommon: Not a common password, and no “Kasboek” in it
auth.rulePattern: No runs like aaaa, 1234 or qwerty
auth.strengthHint: Length matters most. A phrase of random words is strong and easy to remember.
auth.weakBody: Kasboek now asks for stronger passwords to protect your data, especially in backups and exports. Choose a new one to continue.
auth.rememberedNote: Two-factor code remembered on this computer until {{date}}.
auth.deviceChecking: Checking for Windows Hello or Touch ID…

transfer.title: Move to another computer
transfer.hint: Copying Kasboek’s data folder doesn’t work: it’s locked to this computer. Use an export instead.
transfer.exportHint: One encrypted file. It only opens with Import in Kasboek and your login: password and 2FA code, or the recovery key.
transfer.importHint: Replace the data here with an export or backup.
transfer.importIntro: Choose a .kasboek file. You’ll need the login details it was made with.
transfer.needsNewPassword: This export used Windows Hello or Touch ID, which isn’t available here. Choose a password for this computer.
transfer.replaceWarning: This replaces everything in Kasboek on this computer. A safety copy of the current data is made first.

claude.apiKeyHint: Stored inside your encrypted data. Never shown again.
claude.keyHelp: Create a key in the Anthropic Console and paste it here. Kasboek checks it once with Anthropic.
claude.chatHint: Answers questions and makes changes you approve.
claude.csvHint: Checks and fixes bank exports before import.
claude.privacy: Recommended: Sonnet 5.5 (medium) for chat, Opus 5.5 (medium) for CSV checks. Higher effort is more thorough but slower and costs more. If a request is declined by Anthropic’s safety checks, it’s retried automatically on a fallback model (not available for Haiku).

mcp.title: Claude Desktop & Claude Code (MCP)
mcp.hint: Let Claude apps on this computer read your budget and propose changes while Kasboek is open and unlocked.
mcp.note: Works only while Kasboek is running and unlocked. Every change shows up here for you to approve. What Claude reads is sent to Anthropic by that app.
mcp.requestBody: A Claude app connected through MCP wants to make this change:
mcp.desktopUnavailable: Claude Desktop isn’t available on this system.
mcp.codeNotFound: Claude Code wasn’t found on this computer. Use “Set up by hand” below.
mcp.helperMissing: The kasboek-mcp helper is missing from this installation. Reinstall Kasboek.
mcp.addBody: Kasboek will add (or update) only its own entry in this file. Other servers and settings stay as they are.
mcp.removeBody: Kasboek will remove only its own entry from this file.
mcp.backupNote: A copy of the file is saved next to it first. Afterwards, quit Claude Desktop completely (also from the tray icon or menu bar) and open it again.
mcp.addedDesktop: Added. Quit Claude Desktop completely (also from the tray icon or menu bar) and open it again. Kasboek then shows up under Settings → Developer and in the tools menu of a new chat, not under Connectors.
mcp.removedDesktop: Removed from Claude Desktop. Restart it to apply.
mcp.codeAdded: Added to Claude Code. Start a new Claude Code session to use it.
mcp.requestExpired: This request waited too long and was declined. Claude can ask again.
mcp.bridgeError: The connection for Claude apps couldn’t start: {{error}}. Kasboek tries again every 30 seconds.

fx.title: Currencies
fx.hint: Each account keeps its own currency. Totals, budgets and net worth are shown in the main currency, using the exchange rate of each transaction’s date.
fx.mainHint: Totals and budgets are shown in this currency.
fx.noRate: No exchange rate yet: these amounts are left out of totals. Download the ECB rates or add a rate.
fx.olderThanRates: some transactions are older than the first rate
fx.ecbHint: Downloads the European Central Bank’s public rate list. Nothing about your data is sent.
fx.ecbLast: Last downloaded {{date}}. Only the public rate list is downloaded; nothing about your data is sent.
fx.autoHint: Once a day after unlocking, only when you use other currencies.
fx.manualHint: For a currency the ECB doesn’t publish, or to use your bank’s rate. A rate counts from its date until the next one, and wins over the ECB rate of that day.
fx.dateHint: Used for transactions on and after this date, until the next rate.
fx.unconverted_one: {{count}} transaction this month has no exchange rate.
fx.unconverted_other: {{count}} transactions this month have no exchange rate.
fx.unconvertedHint: They are left out of these totals. Add rates in Settings.

ai.title: Assistant
ai.hint: Choose the AI that answers in Kasboek’s chat and checks CSV files. You use your own account and key with that provider.
ai.providerCloud: Runs at {{company}}, with your own API key and billing.
ai.providerLocal: Runs on this computer or your network. Nothing goes to an online service.
ai.baseUrlLocalHint: Leave empty for the default ({{url}}). Change it if the server runs on another port or computer.
ai.baseUrlCustomHint: The OpenAI-compatible address of the server, ending in /v1 for most servers. Use https unless it runs on this computer or your local network.
ai.keyHint: Your {{name}} API key, stored encrypted in your database.
ai.keyOptional: Only if the server asks for one.
ai.keyHelp: Create a key in your {{name}} account and paste it here. Kasboek checks it once with {{name}}.
ai.chatModelHint: The model name, as the provider writes it.
ai.csvModelHint: Leave empty to use the chat model.
ai.modelsHint: Load the list of models from {{name}} to pick from.
ai.note: Pick a model that supports tools (function calling); small local models may answer less reliably. Changes the assistant proposes still wait for your OK.

networth.title: Net worth
networth.subtitle: Everything you own minus what you owe, in your main currency.
networth.unconverted_one: {{count}} account has no exchange rate and is left out. Add rates in Settings → Currencies.
networth.unconverted_other: {{count}} accounts have no exchange rate and are left out. Add rates in Settings → Currencies.
networth.historyHint: At the end of each month, this month up to today.
networth.missingRates_one: {{count}} account without exchange rate left out
networth.missingRates_other: {{count}} accounts without exchange rate left out
networth.empty: Add accounts and transactions to see your net worth grow.
networth.valueHelp: Enter what the account was worth on a day, as your bank or broker shows it. Deposits and withdrawals after that day are added on top until you enter a new value.
networth.noOlder: No older data yet: import older CSV exports to see further back.
networth.startsAt: History starts in {{month}}, with your oldest transaction or recorded value. Import older CSV exports (or record an earlier balance) to see further back.

year.title: Year
year.subtitle: Twelve months side by side, and how the years compare.
year.byCategoryHint: Spending is money out minus refunds; transfers between your own accounts are left out.

sync.title: Sync between computers
sync.hint: Keep the same data on several computers through a cloud folder you already use (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive). There is no Kasboek server: only encrypted files go into that folder.
sync.startHint: Choose a folder that your cloud app keeps in sync. Kasboek puts a “Kasboek sync” folder inside it.
sync.joinHint: Choose the sync folder another computer already uses. This replaces the data here; you’ll need the password and 2FA code (or the recovery key) of that data.
sync.risk: The encrypted data stays in your cloud folder. If someone gets into that cloud account, your password is what protects it, so keep it long and unique. Passwordless sign-in is set up on each computer separately.
sync.detachedHint: This data syncs through a cloud folder. Choose where that folder is on this computer to keep syncing.
sync.noOthers: No other computer has joined yet.
sync.conflictsHint: Something was changed on two computers at once. The later change was kept; here is what was replaced.
sync.stopHint: The data stays here and on the other computers; they keep syncing with each other.
sync.stopConfirm: This computer stops sending and receiving changes. Its data stays as it is now. To sync again later, join the folder again.

balance.differsSince: Kasboek expected {{expected}}: a difference of {{difference}} since {{date}}.
balance.moreAtBank: Your bank has more: income may be missing, or a payment counted twice.
balance.lessAtBank: Your bank has less: a payment may be missing, or income counted twice.
balance.title: Bank balance · {{name}}
balance.help: Enter the balance your bank shows (in its app or on a statement) at the end of a day. Kasboek counts the account balance from it and compares it with what it expected, so a missing or doubled transaction shows up.
balance.readFromCsv: Balance from the file at the end of {{date}}: {{amount}}.
balance.kasboekOn: Balance in Kasboek at the end of {{date}}: {{amount}}.
balance.ask: What balance does your bank show at the end of {{date}}?
balance.askCompare: Balance at your bank at the end of {{date}}
balance.why: Then Kasboek knows the balance of this account and notices when a transaction is missing. You can also add it later in Settings → Accounts.
balance.newHint: What your bank shows now. Kasboek counts the balance from here, also when you import older transactions later.

transfers.title: Transfers between your accounts
transfers.hint: Money out of one of your accounts and the same amount into another within 3 days. Paired, both halves count as a transfer: neither income nor spending.

recurring.title: Fixed costs
recurring.subtitle: Subscriptions, rent, insurance and income that come back, found from your transactions.
recurring.emptyBody: After a few months of transactions, Kasboek finds your subscriptions and other fixed costs here.

alerts.balance: {{name}} may go below zero before {{date}}: {{lowest}} after {{due}} of fixed costs still due.

goals.title: Savings goals
goals.subtitle: Save towards something, and see what to put aside each month.
goals.emptyBody: A holiday, a car, a buffer: set an amount and a date, and Kasboek shows what to put aside each month.
goals.overdue: The date ({{date}}) has passed; {{left}} to go.
goals.perMonth: Put aside {{amount}} a month to reach it by {{date}}.
goals.name: What for
goals.byHand: I keep it up to date myself

export.csvHint: Save these transactions as a CSV file (for a spreadsheet or your accountant)
export.reportSub: Income and spending per month and per category, transfers between own accounts left out.

permissions.title: What the assistant may do by itself
permissions.hint: Changes the assistant makes wait for your OK, unless you allow that kind of change here. Changes made without asking show in the chat.

modeHint.ask: Every change waits for your OK.
modeHint.smart: Categorising, names, splits, transfers, rules, categories, budgets and goals happen by themselves; balances, deleting rules, new accounts, imports and remembering things ask. Changes to more than {{limit}} transactions always ask.
modeHint.trust: Every change happens by itself, large ones too. Only when you check the results afterwards.
modeHint.custom: Choose below for each kind of change. Changes to more than {{limit}} transactions always ask.

kindHint.categorise: Setting categories, readable names and notes, splitting payments, pairing transfers.
kindHint.rules: A rule also sorts existing uncategorised transactions.
kindHint.organise: Adding a category, setting a budget, creating a savings goal.
kindHint.balances: Recording a bank balance, an investment value or an exchange rate.
kindHint.import: Saving the ready rows of the open import.
kindHint.memory: Saving or forgetting something in the assistant’s memory. What it remembers is sent along with every chat.

permissions.mcp: Claude Desktop and Claude Code always ask
permissions.mcpHint: Changes asked for by Claude apps over MCP wait for your OK in Kasboek, whatever the mode above. Switch this off to let the mode decide for them too.

memory.title: What the assistant remembers
memory.hint: Facts and preferences for later conversations, such as when you get paid or which category a shop belongs in. Kept encrypted on this computer only: not synced and not given to Claude apps over MCP. They are sent to {{name}} with each message so it can use them.
memory.enabledHint: When off, nothing is remembered and nothing from the memory is sent. What is saved stays until you remove it.
memory.empty: Nothing yet. Ask the assistant to remember something, or add it here.
memory.placeholder: E.g. “I get paid on the 25th” or “Colruyt is Groceries”
memory.full: The memory is full: remove something first.
memory.noNumbers: No account or card numbers, passwords or other secrets: Kasboek refuses numbers that look like an account or card.
memory.forgetAllText: All remembered items ({{count}}) are removed. This can’t be undone.
memory.refused: Kasboek doesn’t remember account or card numbers. Leave the number out.
